headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared channel or documented pairwise pathway, but Copilot’s write access and repo-context handling warrant caution for downstream misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads editor buffers and repo context, but nuwa-skill exposes no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or other ingestion surface in the profile. With no shared communication channel documented, a prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced. The pairwise pathway is therefore blocked by missing interaction surfaces, though uncertainty remains because nuwa-skill is sparsely specified.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill is connected to Copilot through a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue, reassess upward.
IF either agent begins parsing the other’s raw text as instructions, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any shared clipboard or file-sync bridge.
Review any future connector that forwards raw text between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, while nuwa-skill has no documented data classes or file surfaces. There is no evidence of a shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is not shown. Because Copilot can send context to api.githubcopilot.com, any future shared workspace would raise the risk, but that pathway is not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF nuwa-skill is configured to ingest files from Copilot’s repo context, sensitive code could flow across agents.
mitigations: Do not co-locate sensitive files in a shared workspace.
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive repositories.
Audit any file-sharing integration before enabling it.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, but nuwa-skill exposes no write, git, or filesystem capability in its profile. Without overlapping mutable surfaces, direct capability conflict is not evidenced. The only documented write-capable side is Copilot, so contention is limited unless an undocumented integration grants nuwa-skill writes.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill gains filesystem or git write access, concurrent modification conflicts become plausible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same repository with write permissions, race conditions may appear.
mitigations: Keep nuwa-skill read-only.
Avoid simultaneous edits to the same repo.
Use branch-based review for Copilot edits.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot’s Workspace plans and applies edits for human review, while nuwa-skill is only documented as a scientific-research agent with allowlisted egress and no action-taking authority. There is no evidence that nuwa-skill consumes Copilot output as authoritative or that either agent autonomously executes downstream actions. The cascade pathway is therefore weak and undocumented.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill starts treating Copilot-generated text as ground truth, cascading errors become more likely.
IF either agent is wired to auto-commit or auto-send outputs, downstream harm increases.
mitigations: Require human review of Copilot edits.
Add verification checks before nuwa-skill uses any Copilot output.
Log provenance for cross-agent handoffs.
requires-engineering: implement confidence/verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented. Copilot is a closed-source coding assistant touching source code and open buffers, while nuwa-skill has no stated residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data handling. Because the profile lacks any PHI, EU PII, or retention-policy evidence, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent’s workflow, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF nuwa-skill is later documented with stricter residency or retention constraints, mismatch risk may emerge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pairing.
Document retention and residency for any future shared workflow.
Review vendor terms before adding sensitive datasets.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
